title: Wispr introduces Canto for low-latency dictation in noisy settings
friendlyTitle: Wispr’s new speech model aims to understand everyday dictation
summary: Wispr has introduced Canto, a real-time speech model trained for spontaneous dictation through everyday microphones and background noise. On Wispr’s own opt-in evaluation data it reported the lowest word error rate among the real-time systems tested, while Gemini 3.1 Pro led its hardest broader comparison.
friendlySummary: Canto is built to transcribe speech from real desks, commutes and busy rooms. Wispr says it performed best among the real-time models it tested, while a larger Gemini model did better on the hardest overall test.
whyItMatters: Better recognition of short, quiet and noisy speech can make voice input useful outside controlled demos. The results are vendor-reported, but the disclosed test sets and limits make the claim easier for buyers and researchers to assess.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Voice tools are more useful when they work with background noise and short phrases. Because Wispr ran the tests, independent checks will still be important.
